title: Sovereign deployment simulation plan v2 - pinning & enforcement test harness
body:
Purpose and scope:

This doc defines the simulation plan and test harness for validating region pinning and residency enforcement for Redwood Private deployments. Goal: create repeatable, measurable experiments that exercise enforcement paths (happy path + degraded behaviors) and produce clear telemetry for compliance sign-off and SRE runbook updates.

Key outcomes we need:
- Deterministic pass/fail criteria for pinning correctness across API surface (generate/chat/embeddings).
- Quantified latency and cost delta for strict pinning vs soft-fallback strategies.
- Failure-mode matrix with rollback criteria and automated detection rules.
- Test harness artifacts (scripts, k8s manifests, synthetic workload generators) that can be run in customer-like VPCs or CI clusters.

Background / rationale (short):
Customers require geo‑residency guarantees for PII and regulated workloads. We currently support pinning at request-level and persistent pinning via project config, but implementation has numerous runtime and edge cases (cache hits, KV cache eviction, fallback routing, third-party telemetry endpoints) that need systematic validation. Field incidents show two common classes: silent cross-region fallbacks during capacity constraints, and incomplete audit trails for enqueued/async tasks.

Test scope and boundaries:
- Environments: staging clusters in three regions (us-west1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1) with identical config templates.
- Models: one small generation model (open-7b), one large (open-70b quant), and embeddings model.
- API endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings, routing control plane APIs.
- Not in scope: full encryption/KMS rotation testing (separate workstream), legal contract reviews.

Test matrix (high level):
Each cell is run with deterministic random seeds and repeated N=10 for variance: 
- Pin type: request-pin, project-pin, region-preference-only.
- Enforcement strictness: strict, best-effort, best-effort+audit-only.
- Load profile: steady-state low QPS (5 rps), bursty (500 rps), long-tail (background batch embeddings).
- Failure injections: region outage (simulated routing blackhole), capacity pressure (node CPU/GPU saturated), KV cache wipe, control-plane latency (500ms/1s).

Metrics to collect (primary signals):
- Pin correctness rate: percent of requests served from target region or pinned pool (target = 100% for strict).
- Cross-region-event latency delta: mean/95/99 P90 P95 P99 for token generation and for total request.
- Audit log completeness: ratio of requests with a persisted pin assertion in audit store.
- Cost delta: token-cost and infra-cost delta comparing strict pinning vs baseline routing.
- Fallback frequency and reason codes (capacity, routing-error, unknown).
- Recovery time: time to return to pinned-serving after simulated outage.

Pass/fail criteria (example):
- Critical pass: Pin correctness rate >= 99.5% for strict pin under steady-state and low-burst profiles.
- Warning: Pin correctness rate between 97% and 99.5% for any run -> requires triage and mitigation plan.
- Fail: correctness < 97% or missing >=1% of audit entries.
- Performance regression: 95th-token-latency increase > 30% for strict pin vs baseline -> requires mitigation.

Test harness architecture and components:
- Orchestrator: small Python controller (pytest style) that drives scenarios, collects telemetry, and asserts pass/fail.
- Workload generator: Go binary (wg-gen) that replays realistic prompt distributions (from telemetry anonymized corpus) and supports token-level pacing and concurrency configuration.
- Failure injectors: k8s job/chaos scripts to taint nodes, OOM pods, or adjust Istio traffic weights to simulate blackholes.
- Observability collectors: Fluentd/otel sidecar config to tag traces with pin metadata and export to a local Prometheus + Tempo test stack.
- Audit verifier: small lambda-like job that queries audit store (Elasticsearch/Bigtable test instance) and cross references request IDs to pin headers.
- Cost estimator: script that uses infra cost model to compute delta (GPU-hours, egress, cache hit savings).

Execution steps (runbook-style):
1) Provision test clusters: apply private-deployments/kind-staging overlays for three regions.
2) Deploy runtime build: use image tag build-test-pin-20251001 (CI build).
3) Seed KV caches: run cache-warm job for each region with corpus subset.
4) Run baseline profile: workgen steady-state, collect baseline telemetry for 30m.
5) Enable strict pin and run same profile, collect telemetry.
6) Run failure scenarios: apply region blackhole, run workload at 20% and 100% burst.
7) Run audit verification job and cost estimator.
8) Generate a report artifact (markdown + CSV) and upload to Confluence test page.

Artifacts produced by each run:
- run-manifest.yaml (parameters used)
- telemetry bundle (prometheus metrics, traces, sample payloads)
- audit-verify.csv (request_id, pinned_region, served_region, timestamp, audit_entry_present)
- cost-delta.csv (cost components)
- run-summary.md (pass/fail and notes)

Failure modes and triage guidance (short):
- Silent cross-region serve: look for mismatch in served_region header vs pin header and any control-plane fallback trace. Immediate mitigation: temporary route-policy enforcement (fail-closed) and create alert PD-incident.
- Missing audit entries: investigate audit pipeline (buffer/ingestion), SLO for audit pipeline is 99.99% ingestion. If pipeline lagging >1m, disable soft-fallback until fixed.
- High latency when strict pin enabled: inspect batch sizes, kernel selection logs, and cross-region cache misses. Consider partial pin-offloading (pin to region-edge) or increase cache capacity.

Telemetry retention and sampling for tests:
- Keep full traces for 24 hours for runs; sample metrics at 1s granularity; persist audit verification CSVs indefinitely in test artifacts bucket.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should strict pinning block queued async jobs that would otherwise be routed to a different region? (legal often says yes, but SRE wants backpressure options) -> ACTION: product/legal to confirm (JIRA:PD-4099).
- Acceptable cost delta thresholds per customer tier? We need thresholds to decide automatic fallback budgets. Product to supply bands.
- Which third-party endpoints (analytics, error reporting) are allowed to cross-boundary during test? Need a whitelist.

Roles & responsibilities for running the simulation:
- Test owner: Asha Patel (eng-private-deployments) - overall sign-off.
- SRE lead: Omar Hassan - cluster provisioning and failure injection tools.
- Privacy/compliance reviewer: Claire Nguyen - audit verification and legal criteria.
- Product owner: Priya Desai - business acceptance of cost/perf tradeoffs.

Timeline and minimal milestones (2-week sprint cadence):
- Week 0: finalize harness design and get legal input on async handling.
- Week 1: build and land wg-gen and Python orchestrator (PR 214).
- Week 2: run baseline and strict-pin steady-state tests, generate initial report.
- Week 3: run failure injection scenarios and cost analysis.
- Week 4: consolidation, write ops playbook changes and prepare sign-off for selected customer pilot.

Quick checklist before running any test: 
- [ ] CI image built and tagged in artifact registry.
- [ ] Test clusters provisioned in three regions.
- [ ] Audit store test instance reachable and has test index.
- [ ] Workload generator seeded with anonymized prompts.
- [ ] Observability stack (prom + tempo) up and ingesting.
- [ ] Failure injectors validated in canary namespace.

Notes to self / rough brainstorm fragments (intentionally rough):
- Could drive a synthetic "pin ladder" where requests escalate from soft-pref -> strict after caregiver confirmation; helps measure how long pin persists.
- Collect token-level traces for prefix cache hits to diagnose where cross-region routing happened (cache miss -> fallback).
- Consider a lightweight smoke test that runs on customer onboarding to verify pin behavior right after provisioning.

Related tickets/refs:
- JIRA:PD-4082 (simulation harness epic)
- JIRA:PD-4099 (policy decision: async job handling)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-tests/pull/214 (workgen + orchestrator)
- Confluence: SOE-Residency-Tests-Home (test artifact home page)

Appendix: example audit-verify.csv column schema (CSV header line):
request_id,pin_type,pinned_region,served_region,timestamp,trace_id,audit_entry_present,reason_code,latency_ms

--- end ---

Unresolved: legal confirmation on queued tasks (PD-4099), concrete cost bands from product.

If you run this and hit anything flaky, ping me in #eng-private-deployments with run-id and upload telemetry bundle.
